newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian coffee growers appeal for gov't help.
newsitem.headline: Colombian coffee growers appeal for gov't help.

text.p: Coffee growers issued a new appeal for government help Tuesday, saying rampant inflation and the strengthening of Colombia's peso currency left the country's once prosperous coffee industry on the brink of bankrupcy.

The heads of all 15 of the country's coffee grower committees -- representing about three million Colombians who make their living from coffee -- issued their plea in a full-page advertisement in Bogota's El Espectador newspaper.

The ad lashes out at the central bank's exchange rate policy, saying monetary authorities had basically done nothing to halt the peso's recent rise against the dollar, which has slashed the value of export earnings.
The peso was originally projected to lose 13.6 percent of its value against the dollar this year but it has lost just 1.5 percent.

The ad, which asks the question Is Coffee Growing Still Viable in Colombia?'' takes a swipe at the government and central bank for inflation, which has driven up production costs and is expected to total 22 percent this year, well above the original official target of 17 percent.

It also warns that the National Coffee Fund, which is operated by the National Coffee Growers Federation and guarantees the purchase of crops from growers, is so heavily indebted that it may soon be forced to shut down.

Industry sources said representatives of Colombia's coffee growers led by Jorge Cardenas, the head of the Growers Federation, were to hold talks with President Ernesto Samper late Tuesday and would urge him to take immediate steps aimed at easing the financial problems affecting the industry.

Government spokesmen could not be reached for immediate comment. But Samper has shown little ability so far to influence decisions made by the central bank, which controls monetary policy and operates independently of the government.
